sentences.text: Ilbandornis was an extinct genus of birds about the size of an ostrich, yet it possessed a lighter build than other dromornithids, suggesting it was a fast runner.
The dromornithid family is casually called "demon ducks" because they are closely related to waterfowl.
Ilbandornis were very large birds, with estimated masses ranging from that of an ostrich to twice that weight, specifically between 114 kg and 279 kg for the species Ilbandornis woodburnei.

Patricia Vickers-Rich named two species of Ilbandornis in 1979, establishing the genus in that same year after finding fossils in the Waite Formation at the Alcoota Fossil Beds in Australia's Northern Territory.
Most researchers believe Ilbandornis was herbivorous, supported by molecular analysis of its gastroliths and eggshells.

Ilbandornis belongs to the family Dromornithidae, though some researchers debate whether Ilbandornis lawsoni should remain in its own genus or be classified as a species of Genyornis or synonymous with I. woodburnei.

Ilbandornis went extinct during the Miocene epoch, with fossils dating to the Late Miocene and a record spanning from the Tortonian to the Late Pleistocene, between 11.63 and 0.0117 million years ago.
